job: EVAP vent valve (canister vent solenoid) replacement
unit: per job: one EVAP canister vent valve (also called the canister vent solenoid, vent control valve or canister close valve), near the charcoal canister, fitted. Not included: smoke test or other diagnosis, the purge valve, the charcoal canister, a vent filter or relocation kit, the gas cap, and any hose, harness or filler pipe not sold with the valve

finding: HELD: this file is not ready to publish. There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), and a range cannot be built yet, for four reasons. (1) No maker-stated time for replacing the vent valve alone was found. Every maker time located bundles something else: Hyundai's 0.8 for the 2012-2016 Accent is printed with no unit and covers an inspection plus the air drain case; GM's 0.8 hr for the 2007-2010 Escalade covers the valve assembly plus a jumper harness; GM's 1.1 hrs for the 2011-2015 Silverado is a revised-assembly retrofit with a filter kit and hose; Nissan's Frontier and Titan times (0.9 and 1.3, no unit) cover the canister, filler tube and more; Honda's Accord and Ridgeline bulletins replace the canister and move the valve across. Those are cross-checks only, so the hours for the economy, midsize and luxury classes are null. (2) The only stated one-valve times are a parts seller's approximate figures on its product pages for the Silverado 1500 (30 minutes and 1 hour), so the truck range of 0.5-1.0 hr rests entirely on a seller's estimate, not a book time. (3) Parts: the economy and midsize classes have a single seller (one dealer-parts discounter); the truck parts low is null because the aftermarket valve was found at $113.18-$115.49 on three pages, none of which states that the part is new; and no aftermarket valve was verified as new for any class, so the lows shown for the other classes are discounters' prices for the genuine valve on pages that state it is new. (4) Only one independent benchmark source was found, and it is model-specific. What can be said: the valve itself ranges from about $18-$23 (Hyundai canister close valve, used on the Accent and the Sonata) through $63-$114 (GM vent valve for the Escalade) to a $164.28 list price for the 2014 Silverado crew cab solenoid. The only total that can be built (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks) is the top of the truck class: $164.28 plus 1.0 hr at $160 is about $324. For comparison only, the Dorman valve at $113.18 (condition not stated) plus 0.5 hr at $120 would be about $173. The one benchmark source gives averages of $147-$148 for two models, with shop and dealer prices of $234-$668 on its year-by-year tables. The bundled maker times of 0.8-1.1 hr suggest the valve is often slower to reach than a purge valve, because it sits by the canister under the vehicle, but that is an inference from bundled operations, not a stated one-valve time. To clear the hold this file needs a maker or trade-press time for the valve alone in at least the three classes that have none, a second parts seller for the Hyundai valve, an aftermarket price on a page that states the part is new, and two more independent benchmarks. This is an estimate, never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote usually adds diagnosis (a scan and often a smoke test), shop supplies and sales tax. The same warning light and codes can come from a loose or worn gas cap, the purge valve, a cracked hose, a blocked vent filter or a saturated charcoal canister, and those are quoted separately. On some trucks the maker's fix is a revised or relocated valve assembly with a filter kit, hose or jumper harness, which costs more than the valve alone, and on some vehicles the valve is serviced with the canister.
